ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan’s Money Laundering Control Act (2016, as amended), Company Act (2018, as amended) Article 22-1, Regulations Governing the Registration of the Ultimate Beneficial Owners (MOEA), and associated FATF-compliant directives of the Financial Supervisory Commission and Ministry of Justice.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening against Taiwan’s Economic Crime Investigation Division list, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Taiwan’s domestic watchlist. Enhanced due diligence is required for mainland state-owned enterprise involvement or sanctioned jurisdiction links. Screening must be performed before incorporation and within 30 days of any ownership/director change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: MOEA Company Registration Name Pre-Query System (商工登記公示資料查詢服務)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Traditional Chinese characters. An English secondary name may be registered but is not the operative statutory name. Simplified Chinese only is not accepted. The English name must be a reasonable transliteration/free translation of the Chinese name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, applicant may file an administrative appeal with the MOEA Commercial Affairs Department within 15 days, stating the case number and legal grounds under Company Act Article 15 and the Company Name and Business Scope Regulations. MOEA must respond within 20 days. Subsequent appeals may be filed with the Taipei High Administrative Court within 30 days of final disposition. Rejected names cannot be extended; a fresh application is required.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are conditionally permitted, but a physical lease agreement or registered service office address in Taiwan is required. The landlord must consent to company registration. Shared workspaces (Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Tainan, Kaohsiung) are acceptable for the ASO/SEO agency if the provider allows registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, principally Articles 2, 4, 98-113, 128, 156, 387 and 392; Foreign Investment Act Articles 4, 6 and 8 where a foreign investor subscribes for equity; Business Registration Act Articles 3, 8 and 17-20; Accounting Act and applicable tax registration rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent local government commercial registration authority delegated for the registered office location; foreign investment approvals are handled by the Investment Review Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application for a Limited Company, together with the approved company name and business-scope reservation, articles of incorporation, shareholder and director information, capital verification documents, and foreign-investment approval documents where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Taiwan has no general statutory minimum paid-up capital for a limited company. The capital must be sufficient for the proposed business and operating costs. Capital is normally deposited into a preparatory company bank account after name approval, followed by a Taiwan certified public accountant capital verification report. Foreign capital must be remitted through an approved banking channel and foreign investment approval must be obtained before subscription or capital injection.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved that the Company accept the subscription by each founding shareholder for the shares stated in the approved articles of incorporation and issue those shares upon receipt and verification of the subscription capital. Resolved that the registered office be established at [Taiwan address], subject to completion of premises and commercial registration requirements. Resolved that [name] be appointed Company Representative and director, [name] be appointed manager, and [name] be appointed accounting and compliance officer, each with authority appropriate to the position. The officers shall execute all filings, banking arrangements, tax registrations, and licensing-related submissions required for commencement of business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Company Name and Business Scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce online company name and business-scope pre-check system, or the competent local government commercial registration counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed Chinese company name, English name if used, proposed business items, shareholder structure, and company type. Select business codes covering advertising, digital marketing, translation, localization, and online marketing services. Obtain name and business-scope approval before signing the final incorporation package.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder corporate registration documents and ownership chart
Power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name or business scope is rejected, revise the name or select alternative business codes and resubmit. Correct any mismatch between the proposed scope and the actual ASO, SEO, advertising, translation, or localization activities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Investment Approval Where Required
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Review Administration, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the foreign investment application before the foreign shareholder subscribes for equity or remits capital. Provide authenticated corporate documents, ownership information, investment plan, proposed articles, shareholder and director details, and evidence that the business is not in a restricted sector. Documents issued overseas must be legalized or otherwise authenticated as required and translated into Chinese.
required_dossiers: Foreign shareholder certificate of incorporation or equivalent
Foreign shareholder authorization and power of attorney
Ownership and ultimate beneficial ownership chart
Investment plan and funding source description
Chinese translations and authentication or legalization evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to requests for clarification through the Investment Review Administration portal or filing counter. Amend the investment plan, ownership disclosure, or business scope if requested. Do not remit subscription capital or commence restricted activities before approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles and Open Preparatory Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank approved to handle company preparatory accounts and foreign-exchange transactions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the articles of incorporation and shareholder subscription documents. Open a preparatory account in the proposed company name, remit the subscribed capital through an approved banking channel, and retain bank statements or remittance certificates. Foreign shareholders must use the approved investment route and comply with bank customer due-diligence requirements.
required_dossiers: Remittance records and capital deposit evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank identifies a compliance or documentation deficiency, provide certified corporate records, beneficial ownership information, source-of-funds evidence, and corrected authorizations. Re-remit only through an approved channel if the original remittance is rejected.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan certified public accountant authorized to issue capital verification reports
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Taiwan CPA to inspect the preparatory bank account, subscription records, remittance evidence, and shareholder payment status. Obtain the capital verification report and supporting work papers required for company registration. Ensure the verified amount matches the articles, subscription schedule, and investment approval.
required_dossiers: Lease or premises-use evidence where requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any discrepancy between deposited capital and subscribed capital before filing. If the CPA declines verification, obtain missing bank evidence, clarify the source of funds, rectify shareholder payments, and commission a revised verification report.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, or the competent local government company-registration office for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the company registration application electronically or in paper form with the approved name, articles, shareholder and director details, registered-office evidence, CPA capital verification, investment approval, and powers of attorney. Pay the applicable filing fee. The authority issues the company registration approval and registration number after review.
required_dossiers: Approved company name and business scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, file a written correction or supplementary submission within the stated deadline. Replace defective signatures, correct addresses or business codes, provide missing authentication, and resubmit the complete application. A refusal may generally be challenged through administrative appeal or judicial review under applicable administrative procedure rules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Labor, Banking, and Beneficial-Ownership Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau or local taxation branch, labor insurance and health insurance authorities, and the company’s commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete tax registration and obtain the unified business number. Convert the preparatory bank account into the operating account. Register employees for labor insurance, employment insurance, and national health insurance where applicable. Maintain shareholder, director, accounting, invoice, and beneficial-ownership records and establish electronic invoicing and withholding procedures.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit corrected tax or insurance forms, respond to tax-office inquiries, and update inconsistent company information. Do not issue invoices or employ staff outside the registered and tax-compliant structure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, for business registration and business-scope classification; no separate industrial licensing board is ordinarily required for an office-based ASO, SEO, digital advertising, translation, or localization agency.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate manufacturing or industrial operating permit. The required authorization is company registration and tax registration covering the relevant advertising, digital marketing, information-service, translation, and localization business items.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from project-level EIA for ordinary office-based digital marketing, SEO, ASO, translation, and localization operations with no factory, construction project, industrial process, or material environmental discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No ordinary process wastewater, VOC, air-emission, hazardous-material, or industrial-waste thresholds apply to normal office operations. The company must still manage general waste through lawful disposal channels. Any later printing, server, laboratory, warehouse, construction, wastewater, air-emission, or hazardous-waste activity may trigger permits and standards under Taiwan environmental laws, including the Water Pollution Control Act, Air Pollution Control Act, Waste Disposal Act, and relevant subordinate regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: No special civil-defense or industrial safety permit is normally required for a standard office. The leased premises must satisfy building-use, occupancy, electrical, fire-prevention, and emergency-egress requirements. Fire equipment and inspections are handled under the Fire Services Act and local fire authority procedures; structural load or use changes may require review by the local building authority. Workplace duties arise under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including risk assessment, emergency planning, safe equipment, and required employee training.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance (財政部賦稅署), administered through the five regional National Taxation Bureaus (各地區國稅局); primary e-filing portal: https://etax.nat.gov.tw; company/tax data exchange via the MOEA One-Stop Registration Portal (https://onestop.nat.gov.tw); electronic invoice platform: https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Foreign investors, including mainland Chinese participants, must obtain prior approval of the Investment Commission (投資審議委員會), Ministry of Economic Affairs; mainland Chinese equity triggers the special cross-strait investment review regime under the Act Governing Relations between the Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area, with the proposed ASO/SEO agency business permitted only if not on the negative list. Step 2: Complete company incorporation (股份有限公司 or 有限公司) through the MOEA One-Stop Service; the incorporation filing is automatically transmitted to the National Taxation Bureau. Step 3: The National Taxation Bureau issues the statutory Unified Business Number (統一編號, UBN), which functions simultaneously as the corporate income tax ID and the VAT/business tax ID; no separate TIN is required. Step 4: File Business Tax registration (營業稅籍登記) with the regional National Taxation Bureau and apply for Uniform Invoice registration; the JV must appoint a statutory representative and a service address in Taiwan. Step 5: Obtain the Turnkey digital certificate for electronic invoice transmission from the fiscal authority. Average tax registration completion time is 3–7 working days after submission of a complete incorporation file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Taiwan-incorporated Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture is a resident profit-seeking enterprise (營利事業) taxable at the entity level on worldwide taxable income at 20% corporate income tax (Income Tax Act Article 3), subject to the 12% Alternative Minimum Tax where applicable; no pass-through treatment is available to shareholders; undistributed retained earnings above statutory investment limits are subject to a 5% retained-earnings surtax; dividends to non-resident shareholders attract 21% withholding tax, and no consolidated/group taxation regime exists, so the JV is a separate taxpayer from its foreign parents and affiliates.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not administer a check-the-box or entity-classification election resembling IRC Section 7701. Relevant statutory elections for this JV include: (i) Income Tax Act Article 25 deemed-profit election, available to foreign enterprises without a Taiwan fixed place of business deriving Taiwan-source technical or service fees, under which taxable income is deemed at a Ministry-of-Finance-approved percentage (generally capped at 15%) of gross contract consideration in lieu of branch accounting; (ii) retained-earnings reinvestment election under Article 66-9 to defer the 5% undistributed-surplus surtax when earnings are reinvested within statutory timeframes; (iii) Alternative Minimum Tax 'basic tax' alternative-basis computation with AMT credit carryforward; (iv) unilateral foreign tax credit relief for PRC-source income; the Cross-Strait Agreement on the Avoidance of Double Taxation and Tax Cooperation (signed 2015) is not yet in force, so no treaty-based withholding relief is currently claimable.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅; Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax) — Taiwan's national VAT, administered by the National Taxation Bureaus; imported cross-border services are generally subject to reverse charge in B2B transactions, and foreign suppliers of cross-border electronic services to Taiwanese consumers are subject to the simplified registration and collection regime.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Domestic sales threshold: full 5% VAT registration is mandatory when average monthly sales exceed NT$200,000; businesses with monthly sales between NT$80,000 and NT$200,000 qualify for the small-scale business tier (1% tax with quarterly returns); businesses with sales at or below NT$80,000 per month are exempt unless voluntary registration is sought. For foreign enterprises supplying cross-border electronic services (B2C digital marketing/SaaS-type services) to Taiwan consumers, VAT registration and collection are compulsory once annual turnover to Taiwan reaches NT$480,000. Genuine export supplies (goods or services) are zero-rated with no minimum turnover threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the Uniform Invoice (統一發票) system for all VAT-registered businesses. Electronic invoicing is effectively compulsory: B2C e-invoices must be transmitted to the National Taxation Bureau's E-Invoice Turnkey platform or an E-Invoice Value-Added Center via API within 48 hours of issuance, and B2B e-invoices within 7 calendar days; the platform performs near-real-time receipt and digital stamping, assigning a unique cloud-return identification. QR-code and mobile-carrier barcode integration are required for B2C e-invoices. Failure to transmit within the statutory window exposes the taxpayer to fines per occurrence of NT$1,500–NT$15,000 under Business Tax Act Article 48, escalating to suspension of business for continued violations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available under Business Tax Act Articles 7 and 8-1 for: (i) goods physically exported from the Taiwan customs territory supported by customs declarations; and (ii) services sold to foreign enterprises or foreign individuals where the services are wholly consumed or used outside Taiwan and the consideration is received in foreign currency. For this ASO/SEO localization agency, offshore digital marketing deliverables (app store optimization, multilingual organic search, and localization services) provided to non-resident app developers/publishers qualify as zero-rated exports of services if the contract designates offshore delivery, the counterparty has no Taiwan VAT registration, the primary benefit accrues outside Taiwan, and no taxable use occurs domestically. The zero-rated turnover must be reported in the zero-rate schedule of the VAT return; any local onboarding support or services supplied to Taiwan-based affiliates remain taxable at 5%. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is refundable quarterly through the normal VAT refund application, generally processed within one month.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) evidencing physical departure of goods, where applicable
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for any exported physical deliverables
Inward Remittance Certificate (外匯收入水單) or bank-sourced foreign-exchange receipt proof evidencing collection of foreign currency
Signed service contract with the offshore counterparty specifying offshore consumption and foreign-currency pricing
Zero-rated sales list (零稅率銷售額清單) filed as an attachment to the quarterly VAT return
Zero-rate electronic invoice (zero-rated e-invoice or M-type manual uniform invoice) issued to the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are a priority audit area for export-intensive service agencies. Taiwan does not prescribe a formal statutory grace period beyond operational benchmarks, but tax assessment practice expects foreign-currency consideration to be collected within 180 days of invoice issuance; longer deferrals require documented commercial justification or the zero-rated supply may be re-characterized as a domestic taxable supply. Supporting records (customs data, remittance watermarks, contracts, workpapers, and deployment evidence) must be retained for at least 5 years. Upon a failed substantiation, the tax authority retroactively reverses the zero rate, assesses 5% output VAT on the gross consideration, and imposes a fine of up to 5 times the underpaid tax under Business Tax Act Article 51, together with daily interest from the original due date; deliberate or fraudulent schemes attract aggravated penalties, sealing of accounting books, suspension of business, and criminal referral under Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act (imprisonment up to 5 years) and Article 62 of the Business Tax Act. The general assessment period is 5 years from filing, extended to 7 years where fraud is proven. The authority operates a dedicated zero-rating cross-check program that reconciles customs declaration records, central-bank foreign-exchange settlement data, and business tax returns to detect fictitious exports or exchange manipulations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (the CBC / 中央銀行), exercising foreign-exchange administration under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (管理外匯條例) and the CBC's Regulations Governing the Declaration of Foreign Exchange Receipts and Disbursements or Transactions; banking supervision is vested in the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC / 金融監督管理委員會), whereas approval of mainland Chinese equity investment is vested in the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA / 經濟部投資審議委員會) under the Act for Relations between the People of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area (臺灣地區與大陸地區人民關係條例). The CBC operates a managed-float regime for the New Taiwan Dollar (TWD), with all authorized dealer banks required to transmit settlement data through the CBC's foreign-currency data reporting system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: TWD is convertible but not freely internationalized; convertibility is administered through authorized dealer banks. Current-account flows (non-merchandise trade such as ASO/SEO localization services, advertising procurement, SaaS licensing, and contractor fees) are freely convertible upon declaration; each foreign-exchange settlement equivalent to NT$500,000 or above requires an individual declaration (結匯申報書) filed by the settling bank with the CBC under the applicable transaction-nature code. Capital-account flows are restricted: paid-in capital injection from mainland shareholders requires a prior MOEA Investment Commission permit, bank processing through a declared equity-investment purpose code, and China-side ODI foreign-exchange registration by the mainland parent, while dividend and profit repatriation to the mainland shareholder requires audited profit evidence, CBC-filed investment-income remittance documentation, and non-resident dividend withholding in the absence of an effective cross-strait tax agreement. Practical hurdles include the prohibition on using fintech EMI rails (Wise/Payoneer) for capital-account remittances, the unavailability of offshore TWD settlement, and the requirement that all cross-strait remittances be supported by genuine trade or investment documentation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Taiwan does not impose a fixed mandatory conversion ratio for export or service-export proceeds; proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency deposit account or voluntarily converted into TWD. The statutory discipline is repatriation: goods-export proceeds must be received within four months of customs export release, and service-export proceeds (including ASO/SEO agency fees) must be credited to the JV's designated foreign-currency account in accordance with the payment schedule of the signed service contract; overdue proceeds require a written extension application to the authorized dealer bank with CBC filing. The shipper/service provider must declare the transaction nature at settlement and retain service agreements, invoices, acceptance reports, App Store/Google performance reports, and settlement confirmations for at least five years for CBC verification; no surrender ratio applies to retained USD, EUR, or RMB balances in the JV's foreign-currency deposit account.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Conditionally viable (B+ feasibility rating). Wise Business and Payoneer may be onboarded as complementary collection and payout rails for small-value overseas client receipts (App Store optimization retainers, Google Ads fee pass-throughs, freelancer localization invoices) and for contractor disbursements under USD 10,000 per transaction, provided the balances are swept to the primary domestic bank at least weekly. Legal constraints: neither provider is a licensed bank in Taiwan; they operate as payment/E-Money service providers through local partner-bank clearing, and the JV's domestic bank will require disclosure of these channels as documented collection sources. EMI rails cannot carry capital-account flows, cannot substitute for SWIFT-backed service-export settlement evidence for CBC declaration and tax filing, and must never be used to remit dividends back to the mainland parent, as China's SAFE requires such inbound investment receipts to be settled through regulated bank channels under the parent's ODI registration.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A face-to-face KYC interview at the account-opening branch is mandatory for the company's responsible person (董事長/負責人) and at least one additional joint signatory under FSC customer-due-diligence guidelines; bank officers must verify the original national ID or passport, company registration certificate, articles of incorporation, company seal and chop (公司大小章), tax registration certificate, and the MOEA Investment Commission approval letter where mainland shareholders exist. A mainland-resident director may, exceptionally, participate by video conference when the Taiwan-resident general manager or CFO attends physically, but tier-1 banks uniformly classify mainland-funded companies as enhanced due diligence and will insist on either an in-person appearance of a Taiwan-appointed executive or a bank officer call visit to the JV's registered office. Remote-only onboarding for a newly incorporated JV is not available in Taiwan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mainland China shareholder ownership of the Taiwan JV creating the enhanced-due-diligence 'mainland-funded enterprise' (陸資) classification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: MOEA Investment Commission approval letter for the mainland investment; mainland-funded enterprise registration certificate; board resolution and articles of incorporation; mainland parent's business license, audited financial statements, and tax payment certificates; complete ownership-chain chart down to final natural-person UBOs; UBO declaration under the Money Laundering Control Act; bank reference letters from the mainland parent's principal bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds scrutiny on the inbound seed capital / paid-in capital originating from mainland China
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: China-side ODI registration certificate of the mainland parent (NDRC filing or MOFCOM/provincial commerce authority approval plus SAFE foreign-exchange registration); remittance advice showing that the remitter is the mainland parent's own account at an authorized bank; CBC foreign-exchange declaration form (結匯申報書) with equity-investment nature code; accountant's capital verification report; escrow release instruction executed only after MOEA capital registration is completed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible digital-service business model (ASO/SEO) with no physical goods, raising genuineness-of-business and transaction-substance concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master service agreements and client insertion orders from app developers and e-commerce sellers; monthly performance deliverables (App Store Connect and Google Play Console screenshots, Search Console reports, keyword and review audit reports); issued VAT invoices (統一發票) and revenue ledger; Taiwan office lease agreement; staff payroll and labor insurance records; corporate tax and business tax filing history once available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Receipt concentration through Wise/Payoneer creating an unverified-third-party payments pattern
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Client-vendor reconciliation ledger mapping every EMI receipt to a specific invoice and contract; EMI account statements; written AML/CFT compliance policy of the JV; commitment letter to sweep EMI balances to the domestic bank at least weekly; audit trail of service acceptance reports for each paying client; explanation of why clients prefer card/EMI settlement for sub-threshold service fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident mainland directors or authorized signatories lacking Taiwan ARC/APRC and bankability for signature verification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Appointment of a Taiwan-resident general manager or CFO as primary bank signatory; board resolution explicitly delegating treasury and disbursement authority; certified passport copies and Taiwan entry/visa records of mainland directors; corporate power of attorney signed by all directors limiting the non-resident's control over fund disbursement; registered office and operational presence evidence supporting supervision by the Taiwan executive.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Precondition chain: (i) the mainland parent completes China-outbound investment approvals (NDRC filing, MOFCOM or provincial commerce authority certificate, and SAFE foreign-exchange registration) and (ii) the Taiwan JV obtains the MOEA Investment Commission permit to accept mainland investment. Execution: SWIFT MT103 remittance from the mainland parent's own bank account, denominated in USD or in CNY through the Taipei RMB clearing mechanism operated by Bank of China's Taipei branch, to the JV's newly opened capital escrow account at the Taiwan deposit bank; the receiving bank files the CBC declaration under the equity-investment transaction-nature code (inward investment in an onshore enterprise) and holds funds in escrow. Release: after MOEA registration of the paid-in capital and delivery of the accountant's capital verification report to the bank, funds are re-designated to the operational NT$/USD account and become deployable working capital. Compliance safeguards: no third-party remittance is accepted as shareholder capital; funds must arrive in disclosed tranches matching the approved investment amount; the mainland parent must evidence the lawful exit of foreign exchange from China; any subsequent capital increase or shareholder loan requires a fresh Investment Commission approval and CBC-filed declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: SWIFT MT103 from the JV's NT$/USD operational account for vendor payments above USD 10,000 equivalent, covering Apple Search Ads, Google Ads, Meta, enterprise SaaS subscriptions, and overseas localization subcontractors; each transfer is backed by a contract/invoice and a CBC service-import declaration. Taiwan-domiciled subcontractors and domestic suppliers are settled through the FISC domestic clearing network (ACH-style same-day TWD clearing). Wise B2B and Payoneer serve as supplemental rails for contractor payouts below USD 10,000 per transaction with monthly aggregation and reconciliation to the sub-ledger. Corporate virtual cards issued by the tier-1 bank are the preferred rail for recurring ad-spend auto-payments. Dividend repatriation to the mainland shareholder must be executed only via SWIFT through the domestic bank, with CBC investment-income declaration, after withholding and relevant tax clearance. Commercial Letters of Credit are not applicable to intangible ASO/SEO services, but standby L/Cs or bank guarantees may support high-value annual master service agreements where international clients require performance security.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/TWD forward contracts (up to 12 months) with verified underlying service-export invoices or ad-spend commitments
CNH/TWD and CNY/TWD forwards executed through the Taipei RMB clearing bank for mainland-parent-linked settlement and RMB-denominated costs
FX swaps (換匯交易) for temporary conversion of foreign-currency receipts into NT$ working capital with matched repurchase dates
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCS) for matched borrowing and asset positions, subject to bank credit approval and documentation of underlying exposure
European-style currency options for capped USD/TWD volatility hedging, permitted only against documented trade or service exposure

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): permitted onshore only for hedging real trade or service exposures, executed by authorized dealer banks with cash settlement in USD and CBC inspection; speculative or offshore-booked TWD NDFs are administratively prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 1 May to 31 May following the taxable year; extension may be available under prescribed conditions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a surcharge of 10% of tax payable, subject to statutory minimum and maximum amounts; non-filing may attract a 20% surcharge, assessment by the tax authority, additional penalties, and collection measures. No automatic annual-return strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders; filings, if required, with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once annually, generally within six months after the end of the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or properly document the meeting may trigger fines under the Company Act and potential director liability. No automatic strike-off is triggered solely by failure to hold the annual meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statement preparation and statutory filing support
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce, where filing or CPA certification is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements should be prepared for shareholder approval within six months after fiscal year-end; filing requirements depend on entity type, capital, revenue, employee count, and regulated status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to comply with applicable accounting, approval, certification, or filing requirements may result in Company Act fines, repeated fines, director liability, and tax reassessment. No general annual franchise filing exists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership and corporate information review
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company internal records; competent authorities upon statutory request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Review at least annually and promptly update records after any ownership, director, address, or control change; no general annual public UBO return is required for an ordinary private company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or produce accurate corporate, shareholder, director, or controlling-person information may result in regulatory fines, enhanced scrutiny, and remedial orders. Administrative strike-off is not an ordinary consequence of an annual UBO review failure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate registration change filing, if annual review identifies reportable changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce or competent local company registration authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 15 days after a registrable corporate change, subject to the specific change and governing rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incomplete registration may incur statutory fines, repeated daily or periodic fines where permitted, and restrictions on relying on unregistered information. Persistent non-compliance may lead to administrative dissolution procedures in legally specified circumstances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a private Taiwan company, CPA certification is generally required where paid-in capital reaches at least NTD 30 million, annual net sales reach at least NTD 100 million, average annual employees reach at least 100, or another statutory or regulated-company condition applies. Thresholds and exemptions must be confirmed against the applicable fiscal year rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan IFRS applies to public and otherwise designated entities. Eligible private companies generally use Taiwan Enterprise Accounting Standards or IFRS, consistently applied and subject to applicable Company Act, tax, and CPA-certification requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No general annual UBO filing is required for an ordinary private Taiwan company. The company must maintain an accurate shareholder register, director and supervisor records, ownership and control information, and supporting identification documents; changes in shareholding or control must be documented promptly and reported where a statutory registration obligation applies.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Supervisors, if applicable
Beneficial ownership and controlling-person due diligence records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 1,500-5,000 per year, depending on city, premises, mail handling, nominee or local agent services, and operational substance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-15,000 for a small private joint venture; higher fees apply for CPA certification, foreign-invested structures, complex transactions, multilingual reporting, or regulated activities
